name: Min Cost String
description: Let's define the cost of a string $$$s$$$ as the number of index pairs $$$i$$$ and $$$j$$$ ($$$1 \le i \lt j \lt |s|$$$) such that $$$s_i = s_j$$$ and $$$s_{i+1} = s_{j+1}$$$. You are given two positive integers $$$n$$$ and $$$k$$$. Among all strings with length $$$n$$$ that contain only the first $$$k$$$ characters of the Latin alphabet, find a string with minimum possible cost . If there are multiple such strings with minimum cost — find any of them.
input_specification: The only line contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$k$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5; 1 \le k \le 26$$$).
output_specification: Print the string $$$s$$$ such that it consists of $$$n$$$ characters, each its character is one of the $$$k$$$ first Latin letters, and it has the minimum possible cost among all these strings. If there are multiple such strings — print any of them.
subsubtopic: 406. Knuth Morris Pratt (KMP) and Prefix Automaton
approach_summary: Precompute the prefix function π[i] matching longest proper prefix-suffix in O(M). Traverse text string with π transitions to locate all occurrences in O(N) time.
